answer: Each agent must lock slashable collateral and register one unique utility meter on a public knoll of energy attestations. At unpredictable times the protocol requests a short-lived zephyr reading, signed by the utility, for a prescribed interval. Voting power remains only while the bond stays above a published ridge. If two keys share a meter, a reading is late or reused, or the bond falls below the ridge, every linked deposit is burned. Fielding N identities requires N separate meters, N utility accounts, and N ridge-locked bonds, so service cost and capital scale with farm size.
